key_insight: Neptuna introduces the first large-scale benchmark for shock-driven compressible multiphase flows and shows that no single ML surrogate or loss dominates across all scenarios and metrics.
engineering_relevance: The framework helps engineers choose and validate surrogate models for complex multiphase flow prediction, especially where shocks, interfaces, and multiscale dynamics make accurate simulation expensive.
method: Built a 2.4 TB benchmark spanning 2D and 3D shock-induced bubble collapse and droplet breakup datasets.
Compared convolutional, spectral, transformer-based, and pre-trained PDE foundation models.
Tested MSE-only training against composite losses and adaptive balancing methods such as SoftAdapt and GradNorm.
evidence_signal: Evaluation used pointwise, spectral, feature-focused, structural, and physics-informed metrics, and the abstract reports that composite losses improved interface preservation and spectral fidelity.
watch_item: Results may be sensitive to dataset type and metric choice, so a model that wins on one benchmark case may not generalize across all multiphase flow regimes.
paper_title: Neptuna: A Comprehensive Machine Learning Framework for Benchmarking Complex Multiphase Flows
